answer: Sybil resistance starts with a registration bond that scales with sibling identities. To forge a new key an agent must link it to a separately funded stake, and the required bond rises superlinearly per payer. Bonds are slashable when cosigned agents contradict each other, so anyone who tries to wander across many synthetic personas risks losing real capital on each. Honest peers bridge trust only by cosigning wallets they have transacted with, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand live bonds plus expected slashing.
